claims.text: The originally reported HfNbTiVAl10 alloy has a hierarchical heterostructure.
VEC-guided screening in Nb-Mo-Ta-V-W systems provides an analogue for modifying HfNbTiVAl10.
The proposed intervention enriches Ta and V while depleting Mo and W during arc melting.
The proposed composition change will enhance phase dispersion.
The proposed composition change will refine or more clearly define grain boundaries.
The composition change alters the alloy's local bonding environment.
The composition change alters phase stability.
The resulting microstructural changes modulate dislocation activity.
The resulting microstructural changes modulate crack propagation.
More clearly defined structure-property relationships will improve predictions of Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture behavior.
The proposed approach will reduce simulation prediction errors by approximately 20–30% relative to established methods.
The proposed approach could reduce computational processing time by approximately 50% relative to established methods.
Arc-melting inhomogeneity may prevent formation of the intended hierarchical microstructure.
Processing-parameter deviations may prevent formation of the intended hierarchical microstructure.
The alloy's multiphase complexity may exceed the predictive capacity of the proposed simulation framework.

contradictions.description: The named initial composition HfNbTiVAl10 contains no stated Ta, Mo, or W, yet the intervention calls for enriching Ta and depleting Mo and W. No initial Mo/W inventory or substitution scheme is given, so depletion of Mo/W is incompatible with the stated starting formula as written.
The modified sample is still called HfNbTiVAl10 even though adding Ta and changing Mo/W content would produce a different, unspecified composition.
